type: post-hoc diagnostic on existing calibrated baseline states
questions: Among baseline failures, how often is an actually executed native STOP branch successful at some baseline decision?
Does proximity before the decision agree with success after native historical-node STOP?
Does native oracle_success sometimes report proximity only within a macro-action, with no decision boundary inside the success radius?
control: No new sample, rollout or fit. Verify previous integrity/probe/noninterference gates, raw hashes, exact STOP action identity, pose and native final metric consistency. Keep every cohort separate.
limits: STOP branches contain historical-target selection and controller return, not an in-place STOP. Privileged per-state feasibility is diagnostic only; no learned trigger, exhaustive oracle or population generalization. Existing validation data are diagnostic, not a new held-out test. No support gate is reopened.
